_comment: Gives 'majority' -- the most widely used algorithm, and one of the two that carry the explicit 'Implementations MUST NOT compute 0/0' prohibition (RFC-MACP-0012 4.1) -- schema_version 3 empty-tally coverage. Also pins the INCLUSIVE threshold comparison: an even split at threshold 0.5 APPROVES (RFC-MACP-0012 4.1, Inclusive comparison), which is the boundary a runtime is most likely to implement as strictly-greater-than.
description: Decision Mode: 'majority' fails on an empty tally under schema_version 3, and an even split passes at the inclusive default threshold.

policy.description: Majority vote at the default inclusive threshold, initiator-only commitment, schema_version 3 fail-closed empty-tally semantics.

messages._comment: schema_version 3, zero decisive votes. The approval ratio is UNDEFINED, not zero: the arm MUST fail without evaluating ratio >= threshold, and an implementation MUST NOT compute 0/0 (RFC-MACP-0012 4.1). Under the legacy schema_version <= 2 rule this same message would have SEALED, because 'majority' produced no result and require_vote_quorum defaults to false.

payload.reason: positive commitment attempted on an empty decisive tally

messages._comment: Two decisive votes, approve share 1/2 = 0.5. Every threshold comparison in RFC-MACP-0012 4.1 is INCLUSIVE, so 0.5 >= 0.5 holds and the vote Passes. 'agent://orchestrator' is a declared participant who did not vote; abstentions and non-voters are excluded from the denominator, so the denominator is 2 and not 3. A rule requiring strictly more approvals than rejections is 'plurality', not 'majority' at threshold 0.5 -- see decision_plurality.json, where this exact tally is DENIED.

payload.reason: even split approves under the inclusive comparison
